summary_en: TANAKA SEIMITSU KOGYO raised interim dividend to 19 yen per share (up 2 yen) and revised full-year dividend forecast to 38 yen (up 4 yen to 19 yen per share for year-end), following upward revision of FY2027 earnings on stronger-than-expected orders in parts manufacturing.
title_en: Notice Regarding Revision of Consolidated Earnings Forecast for FY2027 Ending March 2027 and Revision (Dividend Increase) of Interim Dividend and Year-End Dividend Forecast
translation_en_brief:
TANAKA SEIMITSU KOGYO announced on October 30, 2026, that it is raising its dividend forecast for fiscal year ending March 2027. The interim dividend was set at 19 yen per share (increased by 2 yen from the previous forecast of 17 yen), with an effective date of November 30, 2026. The full-year dividend forecast was also raised, with the year-end dividend now projected at 19 yen per share (up 2 yen), bringing the total annual dividend to 38 yen per share compared to the prior forecast of 34 yen.

The dividend increase follows an upward revision of the company's full-year earnings forecast for the same fiscal year. The company raised its operating profit outlook from 1,800 million yen to 2,400 million yen, an increase of 600 million yen or 33.3%, due to orders in its parts manufacturing business performing better than initially anticipated. Revenue is now projected at 47,200 million yen (up from 45,300 million yen), and net income attributable to parent company shareholders is estimated at 2,400 million yen.

The company stated that providing stable and continuous dividends while establishing a stable business foundation and pursuing sustainable growth remains a core management priority. The dividend increases reflect the improved earnings performance in the first half of the fiscal year and the company's commitment to returning profits to shareholders.
